title: Closing the Equity–Revenue Gap: Pricing Pathways for Unmetered Urban Water Utilities in the Global South
abstract: Urban water utilities across South Asia grapple with persistent financial shortfalls and significant inequities in water affordability, with limited tools for reform in largely unmetered systems. In this study, we evaluate non‐volumetric pricing strategies and service reforms capable of improving utility revenues while reducing the disproportionate financial burden of water expenditures borne by lower‐income piped households. Using detailed household‐level survey data and property value assessments from Karachi, Pakistan, we estimate a logistic regression model of bill payment behavior and train a local linear regression forest to model household reliance on expensive alternative water sources. Next, we build a simulation framework using these models to estimate how utility revenues and household water expenditures change for a range of tariff and service reforms, and how these reforms reshape inequality in water expenditures. Simulation results for the current tariff system indicate that coupling full bill distribution with improved service quality could increase utility revenues by approximately 80% by leveraging latent willingness to pay among currently‐unbilled households. Considering two additional tariff systems—one that prioritizes reducing regressivity of the existing tariff system and another that maximizes expected utility revenues—yields evidence of a revenue‐equity tradeoff: shifting to property value‐indexed tariff yields improved equity but reduced utility revenues under both service scenarios. Uniform tariff increases aimed solely at maximizing revenues worsen regressivity, lower payment compliance, and raise affordability concerns. Our findings demonstrate that equity‐focused tariff design combined with administrative and service improvements could enable greater financial sustainability and distributional equity in unmetered urban water systems.
abstract_zh: 南亚各城市供水公司长期面临财务缺口，且在水费可负担性方面存在严重不平等，而在大多未安装水表的系统中，改革工具十分有限。在本研究中，我们评估了非从量计价策略和服务改革，这些措施能够在提高公用事业收入的同时，减轻低收入管道供水家庭在水费支出上所承受的不成比例的经济负担。利用巴基斯坦卡拉奇的详细家庭层面调查数据和房产价值评估数据，我们估计了账单缴纳行为的逻辑回归模型，并训练了局部线性回归森林，用以模拟家庭对昂贵替代水源的依赖程度。随后，我们利用这些模型构建了一个模拟框架，用以估计在一系列水价和服务改革下公用事业收入和家庭水费支出的变化，以及这些改革如何重塑水费支出的不平等状况。对现行水价制度的模拟结果表明，将全面账单发放与服务质量改善相结合，可以利用当前未收费家庭潜在的支付意愿，使公用事业收入增加约80%。考虑另外两种水价制度——一种优先降低现行水价制度的累退性，另一种则最大化预期公用事业收入——结果显示存在收入与公平之间的权衡：在两种服务情景下，转向以房产价值为指数的水价，都能改善公平性，但会减少公用事业收入。仅以最大化收入为目标的统一水价上调，会加剧累退性，降低缴费合规率，并引发对可负担性的担忧。我们的研究结果表明，以公平为导向的水价设计，结合行政和服务改善，能够使未安装水表的城市供水系统实现更大的财务可持续性和分配公平。
